subject: Staggered APAC-1 node swap and hotpatch window — notice and ops plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: sre@acme-corp.com, ops-lead@brightretail.io
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 03:15:00 +0000
Subject: Staggered APAC-1 node swap and hotpatch window — notice and ops plan

Hi all,

We’ve scheduled a staggered maintenance window in APAC-1 to perform a controlled GPU node replacement and apply a safety hotpatch to a small set of affected driver libraries. This is a planned, rolling operation designed to avoid a full-region outage — each AZ will be handled independently with traffic drained first.

Why: We observed rare GPU memory corruption signatures during long-running KV-cache workloads. The replacement + hotpatch reduces the probability of that class of error by addressing a firmware-driver interaction.

When: June 7, 2027 08:00–12:00 SGT (UTC+8). Work is staged across three AZ time windows; your tenant may see a short (1–10 minute) capacity reduction while nodes in your tenancy are drained and swapped.

Expected customer impact:
- Short-lived reductions in available capacity during individual AZ swaps (typical: 5–12 minutes per swap).
- Brief latency tail increases for in-flight requests while connections are moved; we expect these to be within current SLOs.
- No data plane changes or model versioning is required from your side.

Mitigations and safeguards:
- We will canary the first two nodes for 30m with synthetic traffic and enhanced telemetry.
- Autoscale buffers are increased and we’ll enable per-tenant fallback routing to nearby regions if a tenancy sees >15% capacity drop.
- On-call escalation path: Monica -> Vanessa -> Platform Pager.

Attachments: apac1-maintenance-checklist.csv (ops steps), impact-matrix-apac1.pdf (tenant-level impact breakdown), canary-runbook-v2.md (runbook). Links to runbook and HubSpot included below.

Action for customers: please confirm a primary SRE contact for the window (if not already provided) and flag any blackout times. If you have strict maintenance blackout constraints, reply with the required UTC window and we’ll evaluate scheduling tweaks.

We’ll post live progress updates to the runbook link and send a summary once complete.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Ops — Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

---
From: SRE Team <sre@acme-corp.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 04:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Staggered APAC-1 node swap and hotpatch window — notice and ops plan

Vanessa — thanks for the heads up.

A few quick notes from Acme SRE:
- Our primary on-call is Priya N. (priya.n@acme-corp.com). She’ll be available for the 08:00–12:00 SGT window.
- Please avoid doing work against AZ-b during 09:00–09:45 SGT; we have a customer-facing batch job that spans that slot and would be sensitive to transient capacity changes.
- Can you confirm whether the hotpatch requires node reboots only or if any process restarts are expected that might drop TCP-level connections?

We appreciate the thoroughness of the checklist. Please CC Priya on follow-ups.

— Acme SRE (on-call)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 08:11:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Staggered APAC-1 node swap and hotpatch window — ops clarification

Vanessa — quick internal note before we confirm back to Acme and BrightRetail:

- Canary strategy: first node will be replaced without evicting tenant KV caches (we’ll run synthetic calls that exercise long-sequence attention paths). If we’re green at 30m we proceed to the next canary; otherwise we stop and roll back the driver overlay.
- Recovery options: if we see >10% 5xx rate for a tenant during any swap, we will immediately enable cross-region fallback for that tenant and rehydrate cache from the fallback node.
- On the question about connection drops (Acme asked): the patch requires a node reboot — the runtime will attempt graceful drain. Some active TCP streams may be interrupted; we’ll surface connection-drop metrics and a sample trace set to the tenant SREs.

I’ve updated the canary-runbook-v2.md (drive link in metadata). Aditya — please confirm that the automated fallback routing is configured for tenants in the impact-matrix list.

— Monica

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: sre@acme-corp.com, ops-lead@brightretail.io
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Priya N. <priya.n@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Staggered APAC-1 node swap and hotpatch window — notice and ops plan

Thanks everyone — short update and confirmation: 

- Priya: noted on the AZ-b blackout; we will schedule AZ-b swaps before 09:00 and after 09:45 SGT to avoid your batch job.
- The hotpatch path requires a controlled node reboot with graceful drain; you may observe some dropped TCP streams during the short drain window. We will publish trace samples to the runbook and also push an incident summary to the HubSpot deal.
- Aditya confirmed automated fallback routing is active for the tenants listed in impact-matrix-apac1.pdf.

We will begin the first canary at 08:05 SGT and post a live status message to: https://runbooks.redwood.com/canary-swap-v2. If anything unexpected occurs we will abort and notify the thread immediately.

Attachments: updated apac1-maintenance-checklist.csv (version 2 — now includes blackout-aware scheduling).

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
